status: Early: 30 modeled operation blocks, including both sessions-set variants, against the ledger's 57 documented blocks. Modeled coverage is separate from empirical coverage: observations support specific behaviors, while session submissions, deletion, and six of eight update operations remain documented only.
summary: Produces developer COOKBOOK RECIPES for the Learnosity Data API — the DATA plane of the Learnosity dialects. Answers "I want the data": a precise, host-language-neutral procedure for running a server-to-server job against a Learnosity Item bank or its assessment results — signing, the versioned POST-only transport, paging a result set to completion, reading the response envelope, polling asynchronous jobs, and verifying the job did what was intended. For "I want a UX of the data" — an authoring experience, a rendered report — the answer is a different dialect. Empirical integration oracle: its knowledge combines published documentation and direct API observations. It makes no Learnosity calls when returning a recipe. It emits a recipe to follow, NOT item content and NOT runnable code. Knowledge combines documentation with direct API observations. Modeled scope and empirical coverage are distinct; the caller implements and verifies the recipe in their environment.
boundary_rule: The dividing line across the Learnosity dialects is "I want the data" vs "I want a UX of the data" — two views of the same underlying thing. L0178 is the DATA plane for the whole family and covers ALL of the Data API; every other Learnosity dialect is a UX plane over some slice of the same data (L0177 is the UX of the Item bank; a future Reports dialect is the UX of assessment results). Route on that axis, not on which vendor API a call belongs to. L0176 sits off the axis: it composes item CONTENT, the payload L0178 transports — L0176 composes, L0178 moves, L0177 renders for humans.
in_scope: ALL of the Learnosity Data API — 57 documented (endpoint, action) blocks across itembank/*, sessions/*, reports/* and jobs/*. This is the data ACCESS plane: reads and writes both. Coverage is partial today (see status and spec/coverage.md); an unbuilt operation is unbuilt, not out of scope

Thirty of the Data API's 57 operations, spanning every structural shape it has: paged and unpaged reads, synchronous and asynchronous work, writes that replace and writes that merge, a destructive delete, and an endpoint whose two operations are discriminated by a field value. See spec/coverage.md for which are verified live and which are documented only

Writing Items to an Item bank (itembank/items, action set) — including the write hazards that are silent: `set` REPLACES rather than merges so omitted fields are cleared, the response does not echo what was written, and an Item written without an explicit status defaults to unpublished and cannot be delivered

How to page a result set to completion — and WHICH end-of-data signal the endpoint uses, because there is no universal loop: on itembank/* meta.next disappears at exhaustion, while on sessions/* it is always present (it comes back even on a zero-record page) and an empty page is the signal. Each family's rule is a bug in the other: one never terminates, the other silently drops data. The failure this dialect exists to prevent is a truncated read that returns HTTP 200 and a well-formed but incomplete record set, where meta.records counts the page
How to sign and send a Data API request with the official Learnosity SDK, and how the versioned POST-only transport differs from the front-end APIs

How to read the response envelope — meta.status as an API-level verdict separate from the HTTP status, meta.code / meta.message / meta.request_uuid on failure, and meta.versions reporting what actually served the request
Asynchronous operations: which blocks return a job_reference instead of a result, and how to poll them with the jobs endpoint

Asynchronous operations: which blocks return a job reference instead of a result, where in the envelope that reference actually is, and how to poll the jobs endpoint to a terminal status without tripping the documented-but-unreal status default
Rate limiting: per-endpoint quotas over a 5-second window, and how that interacts with exhausting a large result set
The verification steps that tell a developer their job is correct AND complete
out_of_scope: Any UX over this data. Embedding and configuring the Author API authoring experience is L0177; rendering assessment reports for a human is a Reports dialect that does not exist yet. If the request is for something a person looks at rather than data a program consumes, it is not this dialect — say so rather than answering with an extraction recipe

Authoring the assessment item CONTENT being read or written (stems, options, answer keys, passages) — that is L0176, which sits off the data/UX axis: it composes the payload this dialect transports. The boundary is enforced by the API, not only by policy: itembank/items + set REQUIRES a `definition` holding at least one widget, so a write is impossible without content composed elsewhere. L0178 passes `definition` through unchecked and says so. L0176 composes, L0178 moves, L0177 renders
The Learnosity Reports API. Note the naming hazard: the Data API's reports/datasets endpoints ARE in scope here and are NOT the Reports API — two different things sharing a word
Delivering assessments to learners (Items API / Assess API) — a UX plane, its own sibling dialect, unbuilt. The session data such a delivery produces is in scope here; the delivery experience is not

Data API operations absent from the current vocabulary, including unbuilt writes, duplication, session-score reads, and reports jobs. spec/coverage.md lists the whole surface; an operation absent from the vocabulary is unbuilt, not unsupported, and must not be guessed at

Calling the Learnosity API. When handling a recipe request, this dialect makes no Learnosity calls: the caller's own code signs and sends every request with the caller's own consumer key. L0178 holds no credentials and performs no requests
Integrations for any platform other than Learnosity
Emitting runnable host-language code — the recipe is a language-neutral procedure the caller implements in their own stack
